title: Development and Characterization of Decellularized Lung Extracellular Matrix Hydrogels
protocol: Harvest fresh bovine lungs from young donors and transport on ice.
Store frozen lung tissues at -80°C until the experiment.
Wait for frozen lung tissues to thaw at room temperature.
Dissect tissues with sterile scalpels and scissors to remove trachea and cartilaginous airways, and further mince into small pieces (5 mm³).
Wash minced tissues thoroughly with ultrapure water containing 2% penicillin/streptomycin (P/S) at least 3 times.
Immerse minced tissues in 2% iodine solution in sterile distilled water for 1 minute.
Perform two consecutive washes in sterile distilled water.
Transfer minced tissue pieces into a 50 mL tube up to the 15 mL level.
Implement five manual freeze-thaw cycles using liquid nitrogen and a 37 °C water bath.
Fill tubes to the top with sterile dH2O after each thaw cycle.
Incubate samples in DNase solution (10 U/mL) in 10 mM MgCl2 buffer at 37 °C for 1 hour under constant shaking.
Wash samples extensively with sterile dH2O for 3 days, replenishing solution every 24 hours.
Freeze wet dECM samples at -80 °C for 24 hours before lyophilization.
Operate the lyophilizer in drying mode under vacuum for 3 to 4 days until fully dried.
Mill freeze-dried samples into a fine powder using a grinding apparatus and dry ice.
Prepare tissue samples according to step 1.
Treat lung tissues with 1% Triton-X-100 at 4 °C for 3 days, exchanging solution every 24 hours.
Incubate the samples in DNase solution (10U/mL) in 10 mM MgCl2 buffer at 37 °C for 1 hour under constant shaking.
Wash powdered samples extensively with sterile dH2O for 3 days under gentle rotation.
Replenish solution every 24 hours.
Perform lyophilization followed by cryo-milling as described in step 2.1.
Digest powdered dECM samples at a concentration of 15 mg/mL (w/v) in pepsin solution (1 mg/mL pepsin in 0.01 M HCl, pH 2).
Stir the sample digestion process at room temperature for 48 hours.
Maintain the pH of the solution frequently during digestion.
Transfer the digests into a tube and centrifuge at 5000 x g for 10 minutes.
Collect the supernatant from the centrifuged mixture.
Neutralize and buffer the supernatant to physiological conditions (pH 7, 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS)).
Use concentrated alkaline solutions for pH adjustment of the acidic digest.
Store pre-gel digests at -20 °C for further studies.
Fix a small portion (5 mm3) of decellularized tissue sample in 1 mL of 3.7% formaldehyde solution at 4 °C overnight.
Incubate tissues in tubes containing 1 ml of 30% sucrose solution in PBS for 12 hours at 4 °C on a steady rock.
Pour 1 mL of OCT into a cryomold.
Place the tissue in the middle of the cryomold.
Pour 2 mL of OCT on top of the tissue to embed it.
Place cryomolds containing tissues on dry ice.
Snap-freeze using liquid nitrogen until OCT turns all white (usually takes 3 min).
Store OCT-embedded tissues at -20 °C until use.
Obtain 10 µm sections in the cryostat at -25 °C on a poly-L-lysine-coated glass slide.
Transfer the slide to room temperature to allow the tissue section to melt on the slide.
Incubate slides at room temperature for 10 min.
Immerse slides in PBS and stain them with ready-to-use hematoxylin solution for 3 min.
Wash slides with tap water for 3 min.
Immerse slides in 95% ethanol and stain with eosin solution for 45 s.
Hydrate the slides with PBS.
Immerse the slides in Sirius red solution in a staining jar for 1 h.
Rinse slides in acetic acid solution for 5 s.
Dehydrate all slides by soaking them sequentially in 70%, 95%, and 100% ethanol for 1 min each.
Immerse the slides in 50 mL of 1% Alcian blue in 3% acetic acid solution (pH 2.5) for 30 min.
Wash the slides with running tap water for 2 min.
Soak the slides sequentially in 70%, 95%, and 100% ethanol for 1 min each.
Add 0.1 mL of mounting medium on top of the samples.
Visualize using light microscopy at 10x magnification.
Implement oscillatory rheology measurements with a rheometer using parallel plate geometry.
Pour 250 µL of pre-gel solution onto a pre-cooled (4 °C) lower plate.
Lower the 20 mm parallel plate to form a disk with a 1 mm gap width.
Start the measurement immediately.
Measure storage and loss moduli over time at a fixed frequency of 0.5 Hz and strain of 0.1% while heating the lower plate to 37 °C for 30 min.
Perform a creep-recovery test after the storage modulus value stops increasing and reaches a plateau.
Apply 1 Pa shear stress to the hydrogel for 15 min, measure the strain, unload the sample from the stress, and record the change in strain value for 15 min.
Draw a strain versus time graph to show the stress-relaxing behavior.
Repeat measurements for three different dECM digests as replicates.
